@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""
+Demo script showing the benefit of exporting exceptions at the top level.
+"""
+
+# Before our changes, users would have to do this:
+try:
+    from OpenSSL.SSL import Error as SSLError
+    from OpenSSL.SSL import WantReadError
+    from OpenSSL.crypto import Error as CryptoError
+    print("Old way - had to import from submodules")
+    print(f"SSLError: {SSLError}")
+    print(f"WantReadError: {WantReadError}")
+    print(f"CryptoError: {CryptoError}")
+except ImportError as e:
+    print(f"Import error: {e}")
+
+print()
+
+# After our changes, users can do this:
+try:
+    from OpenSSL import SSLError, WantReadError, CryptoError
+    print("New way - can import directly from main module")
+    print(f"SSLError: {SSLError}")
+    print(f"WantReadError: {WantReadError}")
+    print(f"CryptoError: {CryptoError}")
+    
+    # Demonstrate catching specific exceptions
+    try:
+        raise SSLError("SSL error occurred")
+    except SSLError as e:
+        print(f"Caught SSLError: {e}")
+        
+    try:
+        raise WantReadError("Need to read more data")
+    except WantReadError as e:
+        print(f"Caught WantReadError: {e}")
+        
+    try:
+        raise CryptoError("Crypto error occurred")
+    except CryptoError as e:
+        print(f"Caught CryptoError: {e}")
+        
+except ImportError as e:
+    print(f"Import error: {e}")
